title: Priority rubric for transient proxy network exemptions during private on‑prem/VPC rollouts
creator: Maya Chen
acceptance_criteria: A clear 0-100 point scoring rubric exists that maps signal values to priority buckets (FastPass / Standard / Deferred)
Automation placeholder in intake UI that computes initial score from customer-supplied answers and telemetry where available
Playbook pages for each priority bucket with recommended SLA, engineering engagement pattern, and rollback triggers
A small pilot with 6 recent customer requests to validate calibration and false positive/negative rates
Sign-off from Security (SRE SOC) and Enterprise Sales on the scoring weights and playbook language

description:
Summary:
This ticket creates an explicit prioritization rubric for customer requests that ask for network exceptions or proxy-based connectivity work during Private/VPC/on‑prem rollouts. We see a recurring non-bug class of work where customers ship with in‑place proxies, transient edge bridges, or bespoke L4 TCP forwarding that prevents our standard onramp. Without a consistent rubric we risk ad‑hoc escalation, unclear SLAs, and security blind spots.

Objective:
- Produce a reproducible scoring rubric that maps customer signals to priority buckets (FastPass / Standard / Deferred).
- Reduce reviewer cognitive load by converting qualitative inputs into structured questions + telemetry lookups.
- Define required artifacts for each bucket (e.g., Data Flow Diagram, HSM/KMS posture, smoke rollout plan).
- Pilot with recent requests and iterate on weights to minimize false positives.

Scope / Out of scope:
- In scope: intake UX changes, scoring rubric, playbook templates, pilot validation, stakeholder sign-off (Security, SRE, Enterprise Sales).
- Out of scope: implementing full automation in the self-serve portal (separate follow-up ticket), deep engineering remediation for a specific customer (handled in Dedicated ENG tickets).

Signals we will use (examples):
- Customer-stated impact (P0/P1 product blocker vs. advisory)
- Network complexity signals: presence of in-path proxy, NAT hairpins, L4 forwarding, custom TLS termination
- Security posture: presence/absence of DFD, data classification, KMS ownership
- Infra readiness: reachable endpoints, port policies, CIDR overlap risk
- Customer engagement readiness: agreed maintenance window, internal owner, runbook availability

Draft scoring rubric (starting weights, subject to pilot):
- Business criticality: 30 points (P0 product blocker => 30, P1 key flow => 20, otherwise 0-10)
- Network complexity: 25 points (supported patterns => 0-25)
- Security artifacts present: 20 points (DFD + KMS + compliance notes => up to 20)
- Infra readiness: 15 points (reachable probes, tested ports => up to 15)
- Customer engagement: 10 points (committed window + owner => up to 10)

Decision log / trade-offs considered:
- Trade-off: stricter artifact requirements reduce fast approvals but lower security risk. We biased toward security after Security team feedback.
- Trade-off: telemetry-driven scoring is scalable but noisy; therefore we combine telemetry with a small manual checklist for 'proxy supported pattern' to reduce false positives.
- Trade-off: heavier engineering automation (score computed server-side) will require more time; for the pilot we will use a spreadsheet + intake UI visible calculation.

Next steps / action items:
- [Luca] Draft playbook templates for each bucket (DFD checklist, rollout steps, rollback triggers) — due 2026-03-19.
- [Maya] Coordinate 6-request pilot selection and notify Customer Success — due 2026-03-15.
- [Eng (Priya)] Create short diagnostic checklist for 'proxy supported pattern' and sample probe scripts — due 2026-03-22.
- [Design (Eve)] Update intake UI mockups with inline guidance and 'request diagnostic' flow — due 2026-03-18.
- [Security (A. Patel)] Finalize required artifacts list for FastPass sign-off and publish to Confluence — due 2026-03-16.

Pilot success metrics:
- At least 80% alignment between rubric bucket and engineering-assigned priority in pilot sample.
- <15% false positives where FastPass was given but later required >2 weeks remediation.
- Reduced time-to-triage median from 3 business days to 1 business day for requests eligible for automation.

Risks / Mitigations:
- Risk: Telemetry gaps cause mis-scoring. Mitigation: 'I don't know' option in intake triggers diagnostic call and assigns to Standard bucket by default.
- Risk: Customers game inputs to get FastPass. Mitigation: require artifact upload and Security sign-off for any FastPass decision.

If approved: follow-up tickets will include embedding the calculator in the intake API (PM) and a lightweight webhook to surface calculated priority to the engineering intake dashboard (ENG).
